solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: One breaking up light or formal gathering so lovelessly (5)

indicators.note: to gather something is to take it in, so PRIM closes round it
love is O, so 'so' without love keeps only S

annotation.surface: Someone breaking up a stuffy party, or maybe a starchy romance with the love taken out.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'breaking up' social, but it is optical: a prism splits white light into colours. Love as O is the tennis score of nil.
annotation.definitionFit: A triangular glass block bends each colour by a different amount, splitting white into a rainbow spectrum.

entries.clue: A one-time artiste (9)

blocks.note: as in 'ten pounds a head' = ten pounds per head

annotation.surface: A description of someone who used to be on the stage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A one-time artiste' reads as a has-been; in fact 'A' is PER and 'one-time' is FORMER, and the artiste is simply the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Artiste is the showbiz word for a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer on stage.

entries.clue: Hot fire from the US or from South America once (5)

blocks.note: in American slang, to can someone is to fire them

annotation.surface: An American shooting or a hot blaze somewhere south of the border.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fire' pretends to be flames next to 'Hot'; it is the sacking sense, and 'from the US' flags the American slang CAN.
annotation.definitionFit: The Inca empire ruled much of the Andes before the Spanish conquest, so its people and things belong to South America's past.

entries.clue: Requiring change in China, Buddhists may do so (8)

indicators.note: 'in' places the change inside the China, splitting MATE round it

blocks.note: china = MATE, from rhyming slang 'china plate'
to edit is to change a text

annotation.surface: Buddhists in China told they need to change, and doing so.
annotation.walkthrough: China here is a friend: in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate.
annotation.definitionFit: Sitting in silent mental focus is a central Buddhist practice, the path to calm and insight.

entries.clue: Spars with parent boxing in street with son (9)

indicators.note: to box something is to pack it inside a box, so MAMA surrounds IN

blocks.note: the word itself, boxed inside MAMA

annotation.surface: Someone sparring with a parent at a boxing match in the street, son in tow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spars' and 'boxing' conspire to suggest a fight; spars are really a ship's poles, and 'boxing' simply wraps MAMA round IN.
annotation.definitionFit: A spar is any stout pole in a ship's rigging, and the principal masts of sailing ships are the biggest.

entries.clue: Lady could employ one male assistant briefly (4)

indicators.note: cut short, so AIDE loses its last letter

blocks.note: AIDE, an assistant, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A lady of the house hiring a man as her assistant.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a male hire, but a lady's maid is a woman; the male is only the letter M.
annotation.definitionFit: Titled women traditionally kept a personal female servant to dress them and tend their wardrobe.

entries.clue: Naughty setter’s going to enjoy appearing in plot (3-7)

indicators.note: to appear in something is to show up inside it, so HAVE turns up inside BED

blocks.note: a plot of garden is a bed
to have or enjoy, as in 'enjoy good health'

annotation.surface: A cheeky crossword setter announcing a plan to have fun in the plot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plot' wants to be a story; here it is a garden bed. The setter speaks in the first person, so 'setter's going to' becomes I'LL.
annotation.definitionFit: Both describe a child who misbehaves and disobeys, plain synonyms for bad conduct.

entries.clue: Speak unclearly having knocked back double dose of alcohol (6)

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, and a word knocked back is turned round

annotation.surface: Someone slurring their words after knocking back two drinks.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is the drunk's slur; 'knocked back' is a drinking phrase doing a reversal's job.
annotation.definitionFit: It means talking in a low, soft voice whose words are hard to make out.

entries.clue: Morale’s so poor where public flogging takes place (9)

indicators.note: the letters are in poor order and need rearranging

annotation.surface: Morale is so low in a place of public punishment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Public flogging' suggests whips; in British slang to flog is to sell, and a salesroom is where auctions are held.
annotation.definitionFit: Flogging is British slang for selling, and auction houses sell goods to the public in such a room.

entries.clue: Fiddle with projectiles going heavenwards (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom

annotation.surface: Fiddling with missiles launched into the sky.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like a verb, as in tinkering; it is the noun, a violin.
annotation.definitionFit: A Stradivarius violin, made by Antonio Stradivari, is the most famous violin, and violin is informally a fiddle.

entries.clue: Music practice — it may contain hard, boring bit (4,5)

annotation.definition: it may contain hard, boring bit
annotation.surface: A dull stretch of music rehearsal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hard, boring bit' sounds like a tedious part of practice; it is literally a tough drill bit that bores into rock.
annotation.definitionFit: Such a machine is fitted with a hardened steel or diamond bit for boring holes in stone.

entries.clue: Powerful person, one helping to draw the line? (5)

annotation.definition2: one helping to draw the line

blocks.clueFragment: one helping to draw the line
blocks.note: a straight-edge that guides a pencil

annotation.surface: A strongman who decides where the limits lie.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Draw the line' suggests setting limits, which a person in power does too; the literal sense is the measuring stick.
annotation.definitionFit: The word covers both a sovereign who governs and the graduated straight-edge used for drawing.

entries.clue: Embellished lecture beginning to nark dons (6)

indicators.note: take just the first letter of 'nark'
to don is to put on, so ORATE wears the N

annotation.surface: An over-elaborate lecture that starts to annoy the university dons.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like Oxbridge academics, fitting the lecture; it is the verb, puts on. To nark is British slang for to annoy.
annotation.definitionFit: Both describe something heavily decorated, with flourishes added to make it fancy.

entries.clue: Put off agent employed to hold line (8)

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it in your grip, so USED grips L inside it

blocks.note: a rep is a sales agent

annotation.surface: Someone deterred by an agent hired to keep a queue in order.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put off' is the definition in its sense of disgusted or driven back.
annotation.definitionFit: Both can mean disgusted by something, or an attack beaten back by defenders.

entries.clue: Carol’s drinking some tea and dashing (10)

indicators.note: SING takes CUPPER inside it, as a drinker takes in tea

blocks.note: to carol is to sing; the 's is 'has'
cupper, a variant of cuppa, is a cup of tea

annotation.surface: Carol having a quick cup of tea before rushing off.
annotation.walkthrough: Carol looks like a woman's name; it is the verb, to sing. 'Dashing' is not hurrying but ruining, as in dashing hopes.
annotation.definitionFit: To dash hopes or plans is to wreck them, and scupper, originally sinking one's own ship, means the same.

entries.clue: One keen on deserts is most erratic, moving out of south (10)

indicators.note: the letters are moved about
S is taken out of the fodder

blocks.note: s = south, removed to leave MOTERRATIC

annotation.surface: Someone who loves the desert wandering unpredictably away from the south.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deserts' wants to be sandy wastes; it is 'just deserts', what people deserve.
annotation.definitionFit: Deserts are what people deserve, and this believer wants reward handed out strictly by merit and ability.

entries.clue: Carvery offering pan with grouse (5,4)

blocks.note: to pan or roast is to criticise harshly
a grouse or beef is a complaint

annotation.surface: A carvery serving a pan of game bird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pan' and 'grouse' look like kitchen and game; both are really about complaining. A carvery is a British restaurant serving carved roast meats.
annotation.definitionFit: A carvery slices hot joints to order, and a joint of cooked cow is the classic one.

entries.clue: It’s used in branding record and disc (4)

blocks.note: a log is a written record

annotation.surface: A record label designing its brand for a new disc.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Branding' could be the hot iron on cattle; here it is corporate identity.
annotation.definitionFit: A company's emblem or symbol is the core of its visual identity, which is what branding means.

entries.clue: Won glaring competition with revised tour dates (9)

indicators.note: the letters are rewritten in a new order

annotation.surface: A band winning a dazzling contest after changing its tour dates.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Glaring' reads as dazzling or obvious; the competition is a staring match.
annotation.definitionFit: Beating someone in a staring match means holding their gaze until they look away first.

entries.clue: Following border by Turkey, one goes on foot (4-4)

blocks.note: f = following, as in page references
a lip is an edge or border
a turkey is a failure, a flop

annotation.surface: Following a frontier beside Turkey, a traveller goes on foot.
annotation.walkthrough: Turkey looks like the country next to a border; it is a failed show. 'Goes on foot' is not walking but being worn.
annotation.definitionFit: This rubber sandal, held by a thong between the toes, is worn on a foot, so it goes on one.

entries.clue: Romance and alcohol on vacation one’s spent in Rio (4)

indicators.note: vacated words are emptied, leaving only their outside letters

annotation.surface: A holiday romance and drinks while spending money in Rio de Janeiro.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a holiday in Rio; 'one' is a single unit of the money spent there.
annotation.definitionFit: Brazil's currency unit (plural reais) is what visitors spend in Rio de Janeiro.

entries.clue: Traveller must respect this awfully simple diet (5,5)

indicators.note: the letters are put together awfully, in a mess

annotation.surface: A backpacker stuck with dreary, basic food on the road.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes the traveller a tourist eating plainly; the traveller is a driver obeying the road rules.
annotation.definitionFit: Every motorist on a road is legally bound to stay under the posted maximum velocity.

entries.clue: Fan of Independence Day in good article by Hello! (6)

indicators.note: D goes inside the string G, AN, HI

annotation.surface: A fan of the Independence Day film greeting someone cheerily.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Independence Day' looks like one phrase, a holiday or a film; the definition stops at 'Independence' and 'Day' is just D.
annotation.definitionFit: The Mahatma led India's nonviolent campaign for freedom from British rule, the ultimate fan of independence.

entries.clue: Pair cycling around interrupts one who dislikes trouble (3,5)

indicators.note: the first letter goes round to the back
to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so OTW cuts HATER in two

blocks.note: TWO with T moved from front to back

annotation.surface: Two cyclists interrupting a grumpy person who hates fuss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' conjures bikes; here it rotates the letters of TWO so the T goes to the end.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom 'in hot water' means in a scrape or difficulty, facing blame or punishment.

entries.clue: Chinese people with bits of information in Asian city (5)

blocks.note: the Han are China's majority ethnic group
binary bits are 0 and 1, which look like O and I

annotation.surface: Chinese visitors gathering scraps of news in an Asian city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bits' look like scraps; they are binary digits, 0 and 1, read as the letters O and I.
annotation.definitionFit: It is Vietnam's capital, on the Red River in the country's north.

entries.clue: Race, going from right to left? It helps if one has a break (6)

annotation.definition: It helps if one has a break

indicators.note: R, right, is swapped for L, left

blocks.note: a sprint is a short race

annotation.surface: A racer running the wrong way round the track, hoping for a breather.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Right to left' seems to call for a reversal, but reversing SPRINT gives nothing; it is R turning into L. The break is a broken bone.
annotation.definitionFit: A rigid strip strapped along a fractured limb keeps the bone straight while it heals.

entries.clue: Admission made by litigator tackling small problem (5)

indicators.note: a tackler grabs hold of an opponent, so I SUE wraps round S

blocks.note: s = small, as in clothing sizes

annotation.surface: A lawyer confessing to a minor difficulty.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'admission' is a first-person statement: the litigator owns up with I SUE.
annotation.definitionFit: As in 'we have an issue with the boiler', a matter causing concern or difficulty.

entries.clue: New guided tours advance (4)

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all the way round it, so LED goes round N

annotation.surface: New guided tours set off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Advance' reads as moving forward; it is the money sense, as in an advance on wages.
annotation.definitionFit: To advance cash is to hand it over temporarily, expecting repayment later.

entries.clue: To a large extent, show assent about menu’s content (2,3)

indicators.note: NOD goes round the middle
a word's content is its insides

blocks.note: to nod is to show assent

annotation.surface: A diner nodding approval at the dishes on the menu.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No end' is informal British for a great deal, as in 'it pleased him no end'.
annotation.definitionFit: Informally, as in 'it pleased him no end', the phrase means very much or enormously.

entries.clue: Worshipper, I understood, needing to swap sides (9)

indicators.note: the two ends of REALISED change places

blocks.note: R and D, the end letters, trade places

annotation.surface: A believer who has seen the light and must change allegiance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swap sides' sounds like defecting; it means the two outside letters of REALISED change places.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who sees another as perfect puts them on a pedestal, which is a kind of worship.

entries.clue: Failed to observe friend with gin dancing around (9)

indicators.note: the letters dance about into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone missing the sight of a friend dancing about with a gin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Failed to observe' sounds like not noticing; it is not observing a rule.
annotation.definitionFit: Breaking a rule, law or patent means not keeping to it, the rule-keeping sense of observe.

entries.clue: One of the Pretenders with cover of Precious — flipping outstanding! (5)

indicators.note: a word's cover is its outside letters
turned over, so DUE reads backwards

annotation.surface: A fan hailing a Pretenders cover of a song as brilliant.
annotation.walkthrough: The Pretenders are a band whose first hit was 'Precious', so the surface is music; the pretenders here are pretentious people.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang for a pretentious person who fakes knowledge or taste, pretending to be cultured.
